title: The Arkansas River Under Pressure
headline: Follow Dardanelle floodplain, Arkansas, USA across 4 real radar observations
introduction: Repeated spring storms and upstream runoff drove historic flooding along the Arkansas River in May and June 2019. The National Weather Service documents record or near-record crests and a levee breach near Dardanelle. Four radar observations follow the selected local floodplain from 17 May through 22 June, with a 29 May acquisition during the documented river-flood emergency.
conclusion: The 29 May acquisition is during the flood emergency, not a measurement of the eventual river crest. Later observations provide follow-up views; they do not establish that all land or communities had recovered. NASA’s regional optical imagery corroborates the broader disaster, while the NWS report supplies local Dardanelle context. Brightness alone cannot distinguish every wet field, reservoir margin or flooded woodland. No flood-area accuracy, water depth or damage estimate is claimed.

properties.name: Dardanelle floodplain, Arkansas, USA
properties.scope: Focused river corridor, not the entire disaster

method: Sentinel-1 RTC, consistent polarization and orbit per story. Source calibrated power converted using 10*log10 where necessary; existing dB sources are not converted again. Bilinear alignment to the first grid, invalid/nonpositive power masked, fixed viridis −30 to +5 dB display. Statistics are radar response, not classified flood area.
eventEvidence: Documented by the linked NASA and national/regional authority reports; radar observations are not a validated flood classification.
